title: Fix the accounting/operations permission gate on booking persistence

input.requestedOutcome: An accounting-only user's invoice actions (create invoice, record payment, void invoice) must durably persist the linked booking's invoiceId/paymentStatus/history fields, not just the invoice/payment records themselves.
acceptanceCriteria: An accounting-only user creates an invoice, reloads, and the booking still shows invoiced.
No persist helper may call another persist helper with a stricter area (add a check for this).
allowedScope: allotment_v2/allotment_v2.html (smallest region around acctPersistBookings / the accounting persist helpers)
constraints: Confine the HTML edit to the smallest region around the permission gate; LAM-18/19/20 edit the same file concurrently in separate worktrees, merge conflicts accepted by the user.
Never touch package.json, test/**, .github/**, CLAUDE.md, README.md.
No Postgres and no network-dependent prod service reachable from this sandbox.
Any JS change inside allotment_v2.html must be verified with node --check on the extracted main <script>.
assumptions: laCanEditArea(area) is the established per-section permission check; 'accounting' and 'operations' are distinct, independently-grantable editAreas (LA_AREAS, allotment_v2.html:407).

ckCanEdit()/ckPersist() (operations || pier) is the codebase's own existing precedent for a persist helper whose underlying data is legitimately written from more than one area — followed the same pattern rather than inventing a new one.

output.summary: acctPersistBookings() was gated on laCanEditArea('operations') only, but is the shared persist path for booking-side writes made by both operations flows and accounting flows (acctCreateInvoice/acctRecordPayment/acctVoidInvoice stamp bk.invoiceId/paymentStatus/history then call it). An accounting-only user's sibling sbInvoicesPersist() call (gated 'accounting') succeeded while acctPersistBookings() silently no-op'd, so the booking-side fields were lost on refresh. Added acctCanEditBookings() (operations || accounting, mirroring ckCanEdit's existing OR-of-areas idiom) and pointed acctPersistBookings() at it. Also added tools/check-persist-gates.mjs, a static analysis script that flags (a) a persist helper directly calling a stricter-gated persist helper, and (b) any function calling two-or-more persist helpers whose gated areas share no common area — the exact shape of this bug — as a regression guard.

filesChanged.purpose: Widen acctPersistBookings()'s permission gate from 'operations'-only to 'operations' OR 'accounting' via a new acctCanEditBookings() helper, so accounting-only users' invoice/payment writes to SB_BOOKINGS durably persist instead of silently no-op'ing.

Static-analysis regression guard: scans allotment_v2.html's persist helpers for a persist helper calling a stricter-gated persist helper, or any function calling two-or-more persist helpers with disjoint gated areas (LAM-17's bug shape).
Task I/O development record (this task's human-readable report).

behaviorChanges.before: Gated on laCanEditArea('operations') only; an accounting-only user calling it was silently a no-op.
behaviorChanges.after: Gated on laCanEditArea('operations') OR laCanEditArea('accounting') via new acctCanEditBookings(); operations and admin behavior unchanged, accounting-only users now also pass.

behaviorChanges.area: Accounting-only user issuing/paying/voiding an invoice (acctCreateInvoice, acctRecordPayment, acctVoidInvoice)
behaviorChanges.before: bk.invoiceId/bk.paymentStatus/bk.history set on the in-memory SB_BOOKINGS row were never written to the loveandaman_v2 blob; a page refresh reverted the booking to its pre-invoice state even though the invoice/payment record itself was saved.
behaviorChanges.after: Both the invoice/payment persist call and the booking persist call succeed for an accounting-only user; the booking's invoice/payment fields and history entry survive reload.

added: acctCanEditBookings() — new helper function in allotment_v2.html
tools/check-persist-gates.mjs — new standalone Node script (no package.json change)
changed: acctPersistBookings() — now delegates its gate check to acctCanEditBookings() instead of an inline single-area check

details: Client-side write-gate fix only (localStorage 'loveandaman_v2' blob key sb_bookings); no Postgres schema, table, or API change.
Purely additive relaxation: adds 'accounting' as a second sufficient area alongside the existing 'operations'; no existing caller loses access.

decisions: Followed the codebase's own existing precedent (ckCanEdit()/ckPersist(), operations || pier) rather than inventing a new gating idiom for a table written from more than one area.
Kept the diff to the single acctPersistBookings() function plus a short explanatory comment; did not touch any of its ~20 call sites since the fix is entirely inside the gate.
Built the static check as a standalone tools/*.mjs script with no new dependency and no package.json change, per the task's file-ownership constraints.
risks: tools/check-persist-gates.mjs's area-set extraction is a regex/brace-matching heuristic, not a real JS parser; it can mis-resolve an unusual gate shape not seen elsewhere in this file. Validated against all 35 current *Persist* helpers and correctly reproduced the known-good ckCanEdit/poCanEdit OR patterns plus the specific bug pair this task fixes.
The tool surfaced 2 pre-existing, unrelated findings (agClearExecute, tmSaveModal) that are real but out of this task's scope — left unfixed.
dependencies: None on other in-flight LAM-18/19/20 work; the edited region (acctPersistBookings, line ~42877) was not reported as touched by any sibling task at the time of this change.
followUps: Consider separate tickets for the 2 pre-existing check-persist-gates.mjs findings: agClearExecute's agent-bulk-delete mixing sales/operations gates across sbAgentsPersist/sbSeatLocksPersist/ctArtifactsPersist, and tmSaveModal mixing config/sales gates across sbMarketsPersist/sbSalesPersist.
rollback: git revert the commit on this branch (or drop the branch pre-merge). The change is additive-only to a permission gate; reverting restores the strict operations-only gate with no data loss — any bookings that picked up invoiceId/paymentStatus while the fix was live remain valid, the revert only affects future writes' visibility to accounting-only users.
